standard_prerequisites.name: The approximation of a flat and finitely presented algebra by a flat algebra of finite type over a finitely generated ring, cited from the algebra chapter
standard_prerequisites.use: Produces the Noetherian model over which the quotient by the local equation stays flat.

standard_prerequisites.name: Surjectivity of the base change map on the kernel of multiplication by an element, cited from the more-algebra chapter
standard_prerequisites.use: Shows that the finitely generated kernel of multiplication by the equation over the model is killed after enlarging the base ring, since the kernel over the original ring vanishes.

standard_prerequisites.name: Flatness descends along the base change defining the model, cited from the morphisms chapter
standard_prerequisites.use: Transfers the flatness statement obtained for the model back to the original morphism.

standard_prerequisites.name: A relative effective Cartier divisor is flat at every point of its support, and the flat locus of a finite type morphism of Noetherian schemes is open, cited from the same chapter and the algebra chapter
standard_prerequisites.use: Gives pointwise flatness in the reduced situation and turns it into the required open neighbourhood.

core_obligations: Reduce to an affine local situation: at a point of the divisor it is enough to find a flat neighbourhood, and locally the divisor is given by a single nonzerodivisor in a finitely presented algebra over the base ring whose quotient is flat (proof lines 4089-4095).

Build a Noetherian model: write the algebra as a quotient of a polynomial algebra, lift the equation, take a finitely generated subring containing all coefficients, form the corresponding model and equation, and enlarge the subring so that the quotient by the model equation is flat over it (proof lines 4097-4102).

Kill the kernel of multiplication by the equation on the model: that kernel is a finitely generated ideal because the model algebra is of finite type over the integers, the base change map on these kernels is surjective, and since the kernel over the original ring vanishes, a further finitely generated extension of the base ring makes the kernel over the model vanish (proof lines 4103-4110).

Descend and finish: because the original rings are obtained from the model by base change, flatness descends, reducing the statement to the case of a Noetherian base, where a relative effective Cartier divisor is flat at each point of its support and the flat locus of a finite type morphism of Noetherian schemes is open (proof lines 4112-4134).
proof_roadmap: Reduce to an affine local situation with a single equation and spread the data out to a finitely generated model over which both the quotient is flat and the kernel of multiplication by the equation vanishes (proof lines 4089-4110).
Descend flatness back along the base change, then use pointwise flatness of relative effective Cartier divisors plus openness of the flat locus in the Noetherian case (proof lines 4112-4134).
difficulty_reason: The lemma says that for a morphism locally of finite presentation, a relative effective Cartier divisor is contained in an open subscheme over which the morphism is flat, so that the divisor is locally cut out inside a flat neighbourhood (statement lines 4081-4088). The counted proof is a Noetherian approximation argument of the same shape as its companion for H1-regular immersions: after reducing to an affine local situation with a single equation, it spreads the algebra, the equation and the flatness of the quotient out to a finitely generated model, kills the finitely generated kernel of multiplication by the equation on that model by enlarging the base ring, descends flatness back along the base change, and finishes using pointwise flatness of relative effective Cartier divisors together with openness of the flat locus in the Noetherian case (proof lines 4089-4134). It is H2: the approximation layer is carried out in the counted span and the cited inputs are standard approximation, base change and flatness statements.
